title: Unit Factor Method
description: Convert between units with the unit factor or factor-label method, also known as dimensional analysis

components.content:
# Unit Factor Method

## Overview

Unit converting from one system to another can be done with the **unit factor** method - also called dimensional analysis.

The relationship between two different units can be expressed as:

**u1 = x × u2**

_where_
- u1 = unit 1
- u2 = unit 2  
- x = converting factor from u2 to u1

## Unit Factor Method

Dividing the relationship with both sides creates two **unit factors** for the relationship.

### Example: Inches vs. Millimeters
Converting a value from one unit to another can be done by multiplying both sides with the value.

### Example: Converting 10 mm to inches
Using the conversion factor: 1 inch = 25.4 mm

## Factor-Label Method

The factor-label method is a sequential combination of conversion factors where numerator and denominator of the conversion factor fractions can be cancelled out to achieve a desired set of dimensional units.

### Example: Converting 2.5 feet to mm
Using: 1 foot = 12 inches, 1 inch = 25.4 mm
